text:
I reviewed the full repo: package code, tests, fixtures, README, and packaging metadata. The test suite passes: `61 passed`, with one cache warning from the read-only workspace.

Overall quality: **6/10**. The code is readable and well-covered for the happy path, but I would not approve it as-is because there are real accounting correctness risks in ingestion/upsert behavior.

**Concrete Issues**

| Severity | File | Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| high | `jobwatch/db.py` | 70-84 | Older terminal-state snapshots can overwrite newer terminal-state data because stale detection compares only lifecycle rank, not reference time. |
| high | `jobwatch/db.py` | 74-80 | Corrected records with the same `state`, `end`, and `elapsed_sec` are treated as unchanged even if CPU, GPU, user, partition, timestamps, or exit code changed. |
| medium | `jobwatch/db.py` | 31-41 | Any unmapped state is treated as terminal, so future or omitted non-terminal states can block valid lifecycle updates. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py` | 148-163 | Negative `AllocCPUS` and GPU TRES values are accepted, allowing nonsensical negative usage totals. |
| medium | `jobwatch/db.py` | 52-58 | `connect()` always creates/initializes the database, so report commands silently create an empty DB when given a mistyped path. |
| medium | `jobwatch/reports.py` | 58-70, 79-106, 135-148 | Report queries scan and group the whole `jobs` table without indexes on reference time, state, user, or partition. |
| medium | `jobwatch/db.py` | 62-116 | Ingestion does one `SELECT` plus one upsert per row, which will scale poorly on large Slurm exports. |
| low | `jobwatch/cli.py` | 90-103, 121-143, 172-180 | CLI handles only a few expected errors; SQLite permission/corruption/locking errors will surface as tracebacks. |
| low | `jobwatch/cli.py` | 54-62 | `--db` is a global argparse option and is rejected after subcommands, despite README wording that all commands accept it. |
| low | `pyproject.toml` | 13-14 | Test tooling is minimal; no formatter, linter, type checker, or coverage config is declared for active development. |

Estimated significant rewrite/change: **about 140 LOC**. Most of that is in `db.py` for deterministic upsert semantics, schema/index changes, and batching, plus parser validation and CLI error handling.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this PR as-is.**

issues.description: Older terminal-state snapshots can overwrite newer terminal-state data because stale detection compares only lifecycle rank, not reference time.
Corrected records with the same state, end, and elapsed seconds are treated as unchanged even when other accounting fields changed.
Unmapped job states are treated as terminal, which can block valid updates from omitted non-terminal states.
Negative CPU and GPU allocations are accepted and can produce negative usage totals.
Opening a database always creates it, so report commands silently create empty databases for mistyped paths.
Report queries lack supporting indexes and will scan/group the full jobs table as data grows.
Ingestion performs per-row SELECT and upsert operations, which will scale poorly for large exports.
SQLite permission, corruption, and locking errors are not handled and will produce tracebacks.
The global --db option is rejected after subcommands despite documentation saying all commands accept it.
Development tooling declares pytest only, with no formatter, linter, type checker, or coverage configuration.
